title: I open-sourced the cozy pixel-art game Opus 5.5 made for me & my friends: here's the repo and a playable demo
author: poookee
selftext:
A couple of days ago I posted this game I made with Claude Opus 5.5 for me and my friends, and a lot of you asked for the repo. So here it is, fully open source (MIT).

* A cozy life in a seaside village plus a 10-chapter adventure, 8 heroes, dungeons and bosses
* Play solo, or with up to 8 friends: on the same screen with phones as controllers, or online from home
* Everything is made in code: there isn't a single image or sound file in the repo

Since code has no value anymore, here's the full repo and playable demo ! =)

  
**Play the game in your browser :** 

[https://hearthlight.github.io/](https://hearthlight.github.io/)

**Repo :**   
  
[https://github.com/Hearthlight](https://github.com/Hearthlight)  
  
(There's also a desktop app for Mac/Windows/Linux in the releases, where Party Mode works offline over Wi-Fi.)  
  
Disclaimer : I did not have time to play through the whole game, it might have bug or you could get stuck !

Hope you guys enjoy it. Open an issue if you want some improvement, I will spank Claude until it fixes it

replies.author: Every-Prize4720
replies.body: im like oldschool non agent developer. anyway how does agent manage changes. you tell it to change relatively small thing can it pin point exactly what to do or is it shooting with shotgun?

replies.author: poookee
replies.body:
Yeah basically you give it access to the whole codebase, and the main agent and its subagents change what they need to. You just ask what you want, you don't even need to be super accurate, just tell them to document your preference along the way.  
  
Then they edit the file you need quite precisely.

Remember, this whole thing was basically built by agents in 48h, so you can only imagine how fast they're going.

replies.author: poookee
replies.body:
I started saturday afternoon, played the first version in the evening after a few hours, then I made opus 5.5 work all night to have a better story and bigger map. And then one more night to make the repo sharable and the online version.. so all together around 48h

I deliberately gave vague instructions about the storyline and maps so I could actually play it and discover the game by playing myself (it’s not as fun to play if you already know the ending)

So I still have to find time to actually play it ‘till the end. im sure there are still plenty of improvements to make, but I’m still baffled by the result, even thoug i’ve been vibecoding since april, it’s crazy

comments.author: mirageofstars
comments.body:
Looks super cute! 

Can you share more about how you told Opus to work all night? I'm finding game dev to still be very iterative and require a lot of decisions and direction. It could be bc I'm picky, though.

When you say it took 48h was that start to finish calendar-time? Or like 48 actual working hours (eg 4 hours a day for 12 days)?

replies.author: poookee
replies.body:
Sure ! So I already explained a bit in other comment, but I was vague on purpose in the prompting, because I wanted to actually discover the game by playing. Right now I'm still not sure what the whole story is about or what all area looks like : I thought it would be fun to discover the game myself with friends, that's why I started it in the first place

In order to make claude work for a long period of time, it's easy I just use the /loop command, and tell it to work until he things the game is good enough. Basically you could tell it something like  
  
\-  /loop Improve the game until the map is the size of the map of world of warcraft, make it fun, don't stop until you think the game is playable for me. And it can just go for hours and hours

Of course Claude Max x 20 is almost like unlimited token, so that's why I allow it to do that, it's not the same if you're on a budget.

My guess would be that I didn't send more than 20-30 prompts total

comments.author: WarKuarto
comments.body: Any recomendations to get a really good quality and related to the style of the game, sprites, with this kind of AI models??

replies.author: poookee
replies.body:
I think it's pretty good at "copying" a style, so if you know a game with a style you like, send screenshots when starting to explain what you like, and make it iterate a few mockup until it looks good.

When the art style is good, then tell it to conserve this for the rest of the game

If you don't have assets to give it, just use chatGPT image generation to iterate and get what you want, it's incredibly good for basically any reference image.

For exemple, ask chatgpt to create a moodboard for your game with the art style you like and different variation, it's an excellent start
